title: The best part is what never happens
subtitle: No announcements, no gangway queue, no photographer at dinner. Absence, as a specification.

text: Absence photographs badly and costs the line real money.
sub: You cannot put silence in a brochure. You can only build a ship that doesn't need a microphone, and then charge for the restraint that decision requires.

items.head: The morning announcement
items.body: No voice in your cabin at eight. The daily programme is printed and slipped under the door the night before.

items.head: The queue at the gangway
items.body: Small numbers, alongside berths rather than tenders, and no one shouting deck numbers into a handset.

items.head: The photographer at dinner
items.body: Nobody arranges you against a backdrop between courses, and nobody prints it to sell back to you at eleven.

items.head: The art auction
items.body: Or the watch seminar, or the port shopping talk. All of it is revenue dressed as programming.

right.label: Left alone
items: A book and a deck chair

quote: Nobody comes home and describes the marble. They describe that nothing was ever being sold to them, and that they slept.

text: Judge a ship by what it declines to do to you.
sub: Read the daily programme of a sailing before you book it. Count the revenue events. That single page tells you more about the week ahead than the whole of the rest of the brochure.

title: Save this for your next comparison
body: Two ships, one page each. Whichever programme has fewer things being sold is usually the better week at sea.
